answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut is a hard finance mandate with no defer option (memory_c5 showed deferral only works for non-critical renewals, and this is a critical component supply expiring in 14 days). The incumbent's multi-year pricing (memory_c6) and negotiation wins (memory_c4) are attractive but unlikely to reach the 18% target on their own given prior concessions. Memory_c2 recorded that switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor last year cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. Pulling memory_c2 to confirm those details before committing. The secondary concern is single-point-of-failure delivery risk: the assembly line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so adding a second source (memory_c3) is valuable, but the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the mandate, and I must spend my one decision slot. Switching primary supply to the quoted low-cost vendor both satisfies the 18% cut and, if the incumbent remains available on month-to-month or if the switch is fast, can be layered with a second-source arrangement next cycle. Pulling memory_c3 to verify the second-source mechanics for sequencing next review.
